name: 音书 (Yinshu)
developer: Guangzhou Voibook Technology Co., Ltd. (广州音书科技有限公司)
oneLine: A Chinese communication app for deaf people from Guangzhou, on the App Store since 2017: speech within 4 metres to text, captioned phone and in-app video calls, captions projected onto a big screen, and AI scoring to practise Mandarin pronunciation.

platforms.text: iPhone, iPad, Android; Mac and Vision Pro
platforms.detail: The App Store lists iPhone, iPad, Mac (Apple M1 or later) and Apple Vision. Voibook's Android download link goes to Tencent's MyApp store. A web page for showing captions on a big screen signs in by scanning a QR code with the app.

deviceRequirements.detail: iPhone and iPad need iOS 15 or later; a Mac needs macOS 12 and an Apple M1 chip or later. Android requirements are not stated.

roomCaptions.detail: Captions speech within about 4 metres, and sound from a TV, computer or speaker, in meetings, training, classes and when you are out.

groupConversations.text: One phone; captions on a big screen
groupConversations.detail: One phone picks up what each person within 4 metres says. For large meetings and lectures, the caption display mode (字幕速记) projects the text onto a big screen or a laptop, readable from 10 metres away. Showing who is talking is not described.

languages.detail: Voibook's pages don't list which spoken languages the captions recognise. A July 2023 update added a dialect service without naming the dialects. The app is in Simplified and Traditional Chinese, and its speech training is for Mandarin.

offline.detail: The September 2023 release notes added offline speech recognition and an offline lifetime card (离线终身卡). The pages don't say what works offline or what the card costs.

speakerLabels.detail: Yinshu's feature lists on the App Store and Voibook's caption services page don't say the captions show who is talking.

voiceNames.detail: No page describes learning people's voices or showing their names.

speakerDirection.detail: No page describes showing where a voice comes from.

translation.detail: In Yinshu's own wording, 翻译 ("translation") means turning speech into text. No page describes translating between languages.

saveTranscripts.detail: Yinshu's feature lists on the App Store and Voibook's caption services page don't describe saving or reopening transcripts.

export.detail: Yinshu's feature lists on the App Store and Voibook's caption services page don't describe exporting or sharing transcripts.

fileUpload.detail: The privacy policy says you can upload videos and cached audio or video files for speech-to-text once photo access is allowed. No feature page describes file transcription.

customWords.detail: No page describes adding your own words or names.

display.detail: No page describes caption size or colour settings. A handwriting board has slider and zoom modes.

soundAlerts.detail: Yinshu's feature lists on the App Store and Voibook's caption services page don't mention alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm.

phoneCalls.detail: Voibook lists phone call captions ("see" the other person's voice), and the Android listing describes a phone assistant. The privacy policy says the app can place calls without the phone's dialler. How it works on iPhone and what it costs are not stated.

videoCalls.detail: Video calls inside Yinshu with family and friends: the other person's speech is shown as text, and your typed text is turned into speech for them. Captioned calls work between users who follow each other, in three modes. Captions for other apps' video calls are not described.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Floating captions are described for livestreams, Douyin and the news. The listing also covers TV, computer and speaker sound picked up by the microphone. The pages don't say whether floating captions work on iPhone.

humanCaptioners.detail: No page describes people writing the app's captions. Voibook offers sign language interpreters as a separate service.

signLanguage.detail: The release notes mention a text-to-sign-language screen in the app. Voibook also offers online and in-person sign language interpreting and sign language training to institutions and individuals; prices are not stated.

privacy.detail: The privacy policy (February 2023) says personal information collected in China is stored in China. Speech recognition and pronunciation scoring use iFlytek and AISpeech SDKs, and voice data is also used to improve the service. It lists advertising SDKs, and the App Store label lists identifiers and usage data used for tracking. Offline recognition is available.

account.text: Yes, with a mobile phone number
account.detail: Creating an account needs a mobile phone number and a username. A WeChat, Weibo, QQ or Apple account can be linked for sign-in.

availability.text: Made for China; App Store elsewhere too
availability.detail: The app and website are in Chinese, and Voibook's Android download goes to Tencent's MyApp store. The App Store also lists the app outside mainland China, for example in the US store.

freePlan.detail: Free to download, with in-app top-ups. Release notes mention timed translation, extra time for watching videos and a yearly card, but no page says how much is free.

price.detail: China App Store in-app purchases, November 2026: top-ups of CNY 8, 15, 38, 58 and 98 (labelled 3 to 98 yuan of credit). The pages don't say what each top-up buys.

accessibilityFunding.detail: Voibook sells caption and sign language services to schools, government service centres, hospitals and other public services, but no page describes a public programme that pays for the app for individuals.

strengths.text: Speech training scores your Mandarin pronunciation with AI, in pinyin, words, sentences and whole texts.
Phone call captions and in-app video calls where the other person's speech becomes text and your typed text is read out to them.
The caption display mode projects live text onto a big screen or laptop for lectures and large meetings.
Offline speech recognition was added in 2023.

limits.text: Voibook's pages don't list which spoken languages or dialects the captions recognise, and describe no translation between languages.
An account needs a mobile phone number.
The privacy policy lists advertising SDKs, and the App Store label lists data used for tracking.
Its pages don't describe saving, exporting or summarising transcripts.

notes: Wording: in Yinshu's pages 翻译 ('translation', as in 远距离翻译 and 悬浮翻译) means speech-to-text, not translation between languages; the table treats it that way. Versions: the App Store (China) shows 7.9.0 (3 April 2026), Tencent MyApp shows Android 8.5.0 (28 September 2026), the website footer says 7.6.5. The App Store and MyApp descriptions say it is the internet tool most deaf people in China use, and the about page gives user and institution counts; not used (no user counts). Pricing: the only prices found are the China App Store top-ups (充值3元 CNY 8, 充值6元 CNY 8, 充值12元 CNY 15, 充值30元 CNY 38, 充值50元 CNY 58, 充值98元 CNY 98); what they buy is not stated. Release notes mention timed translation (May 2023), a yearly card and a dialect service (July 2023), earning time by watching videos (September 2023), offline recognition and an offline lifetime card (September 2023). Conflict: Tencent MyApp marks the Android app '无广告' (no ads) from its own scan, while the privacy policy (27 February 2023) lists advertising SDKs (优量汇, TopOn, 穿山甲, 快手联盟, 百度联盟). Android: Voibook's download button links to Tencent MyApp; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voibook.voicebook returned 404 on 2026-11-02; other Chinese Android stores were not checked. App Store availability: the lookup API returned the app for China, the US, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore (US cited). Not found: caption languages, saving, export, summaries, display settings, sound alerts, speaker labels, file transcription beyond the privacy policy line, any public funding for individuals. Not compared: the Yinshu watch app, the AI training app (音书AI训练) and the WeChat mini program. The video tutorial page rendered empty, and the caption display web page (pro.voibook.com) needs a QR login. How opened: voibook.com is a JavaScript app, read in a browser (the product pages each opened by URL and reload); the privacy policy, App Store page, lookup API and MyApp listing with curl. All checked 2026-11-02.
